sector: Consumer Discretionary - Hotels, Restaurants & Leisure (Hotel Franchising/Management)
overview: IHG Hotels & Resorts is a global hospitality company that franchises and manages hotels under a portfolio of 20-21 brands (InterContinental, Holiday Inn, Crowne Plaza, Regent, Six Senses, Kimpton, Hotel Indigo, voco, Ruby, Garner and others), operating more than 6,900-7,100 hotels (over one million rooms) in over 100 countries as of 2025/2026, with an additional ~2,300-2,400 hotel development pipeline. IHG is almost entirely asset-light: it owns or leases less than 1% of its system by room count, earning fee-based income from third-party hotel owners rather than operating the hotels itself. Reporting currency is US dollars (presented in millions), though the shares trade on the LSE in GBp and as ADRs on the NYSE.

business_model.summary: IHG makes money almost entirely from fees charged to independent, third-party hotel owners for the right to use its brands, loyalty programme (IHG One Rewards) and enterprise platform (franchise fees), plus base and incentive management fees on the smaller number of hotels it manages on owners' behalf. A large portion of reported total revenue is not IHG's own economics: the 'System Fund' (assessments owners pay for marketing, reservations and loyalty, $1,717m in FY2025) and 'reimbursable revenue' (payroll and other costs reimbursed at managed hotels, $1,004m in FY2025) pass through the P&L largely at breakeven and should be excluded when assessing profitability. The metric that matters is 'Fee business revenue' ($1,897m in FY2025, generating $1,231m of operating profit) plus a small owned & leased contribution ($544m revenue, $43m profit from <1% of the system). Total reported revenue of $5,189m in FY2025 is therefore a materially inflated proxy for IHG's actual earnings power; 'revenue from reportable segments' ($2,468m) and 'operating profit from reportable segments' ($1,265m) are the non-GAAP measures management and analysts actually use. Because fee revenue scales with RevPAR (revenue per available room) and the number of fee-paying rooms in the system, rather than with capital IHG deploys, the model requires very little incremental capital and generates high returns on invested capital.

revenue_streams.name: Franchise fees (% of hotel rooms revenue)
revenue_streams.description: Royalty on RevPAR x rooms; ~73% of system size is franchised, concentrated in Americas Essentials/midscale brands

revenue_streams.name: Management fees (base + incentive)
revenue_streams.description: Fixed % of total hotel revenue plus a share of gross operating profit; ~27% of system size, concentrated in Luxury & Lifestyle and EMEAA/Greater China

revenue_streams.name: Ancillary fee streams
revenue_streams.description: Co-branded credit cards, loyalty point sales, branded residences; high incremental margin, a key driver of fee margin expansion

revenue_streams.name: System Fund revenue (pass-through)
revenue_streams.description: $1,717m in FY2025; marketing/reservation/loyalty assessments collected from owners and spent on their behalf, not managed for IHG surplus/deficit

revenue_streams.name: Reimbursable revenue (pass-through)
revenue_streams.description: $1,004m in FY2025; payroll and other costs reimbursed by owners at managed hotels, recognised at breakeven

revenue_streams.name: Owned & leased hotels
revenue_streams.description: $544m revenue / $43m profit in FY2025 from the <1% of system size IHG owns outright; structurally shrinking as a share of the business

business_model.customer_type: B2B - thousands of independent and institutional hotel owners/franchisees (via IHG Owners Association); end consumers interact with the brands/loyalty programme but are not IHG's direct fee-paying customers
business_model.geographic_mix: System size: Americas 52%, EMEAA 28%, Greater China 20% (FY2025); pipeline skews more to EMEAA (34%) and Greater China (35%) than current system, signalling a geographic growth tilt away from the more mature Americas base
business_model.recurring_vs_transactional: Predominantly recurring: franchise/management fees recur for the life of long-dated (often 10-20+ year) contracts and scale with RevPAR and room count; key money and recyclable investments are the main transactional/capital-intensive exception

competitive_position.market_position: One of the 'top five' global branded hotel groups (with Marriott, Hilton, Wyndham, Accor), which together hold roughly a quarter of global room supply in a still-fragmented industry (57% of rooms globally are affiliated with any chain, branded or independent). IHG is generally viewed as the smallest of the 'big three' US-anchored global franchisors (Marriott, Hilton, IHG) by system size and scale, though it has a long-established Essentials (Holiday Inn) base in the Americas and growing exposure in Luxury & Lifestyle and EMEAA/Greater China.

moat_factors.description: IHG One Rewards has 160m+ members generating 66% of global room nights; scale of membership raises owner conversion incentive and guest retention, reinforcing itself as the system grows

20-21 brands spanning Luxury & Lifestyle to Essentials/Suites lets IHG capture demand across price points and converts owners of competing or independent hotels, but brand power varies a lot by segment (Holiday Inn is a mass-market workhorse, not a premium differentiator)
Long-dated contracts, conversion costs, and loyalty/technology integration create stickiness, but owners can and do switch brand affiliation at contract renewal if returns disappoint

moat_factors.factor: Scale/cost advantages in distribution and technology
moat_factors.description: Centralized reservation systems, revenue management AI, and a shared System Fund let IHG spread marketing/technology costs across a huge, growing room base - a barrier smaller/independent operators cannot easily replicate

Building a globally recognised brand, loyalty programme and distribution platform at scale is expensive and slow, protecting incumbents, though this does not stop regional or boutique competitors from eroding share in specific markets

weaknesses: Smaller scale than Marriott and Hilton in absolute system size, which can translate into lower relative owner economics and negotiating leverage in some markets
Highly fragmented hotel industry (57% of global rooms are branded) means intense competition for both guest demand and owner signings against peers all pursuing similar conversion/pipeline strategies
No control over day-to-day operations or costs at franchised hotels (73% of system), leaving IHG exposed to inconsistent guest experience and quality risk at properties it does not manage

Heavy reliance on continued net system growth and RevPAR; a sustained slowdown in either materially slows the entire fee-based earnings algorithm since IHG has little ability to offset weak top-line via cost cuts (opex is already lean)

Negative shareholders' equity (-$2.7bn at FY2025, -$3.0bn at H1 FY2026) from years of debt-funded buybacks leaves no balance-sheet buffer; the capital structure is reliant on continued strong cash generation

growth_drivers: Rooms pipeline of ~2,300-2,400 hotels (339,526-348,000 rooms), representing roughly 33% of current system size - the primary visible forward growth indicator
Record development activity: 443 hotel openings in FY2025 (record) and 694 signings; H1 2026 openings/signings both up organically

Conversion-led growth: quick-to-market conversions generated over 50% of FY2025 room openings as independent owners seek fast access to IHG's platform, loyalty and technology at low incremental capital cost to IHG

Expansion in Luxury & Lifestyle (14% of system, 22% of pipeline) via Six Senses, Regent, Kimpton, Vignette Collection and the 2025 acquisition of Ruby (premium urban lifestyle/micro-hotel brand), plus the new Noted Collection premium brand launched in 2026

Newer/smaller brands (Garner, voco, Atwell Suites, avid, Noted Collection - 10 brands launched/acquired in the past decade) now ~10% of system size but 22% of pipeline, indicating an outsized share of future growth

Geographic expansion into high-growth Asia-Pacific and Middle East markets (surpassed 50 open hotels in India, 800+ in Greater China, growing Saudi Arabia presence), aligned with Oxford Economics forecasts of Asia-Pacific/Middle East reaching 45% of global travel nights by 2035

Ancillary fee stream growth: co-branded credit cards (high single-digit card member growth), loyalty point sales, and branded residences - all high incremental-margin revenue that drives fee margin expansion
AI-enabled revenue management, CRM and content platforms expected to lift direct bookings, ancillary monetisation (upsell revenue already adding ~$20-50 per stay) and operating efficiency

Long-term structural industry tailwinds: branded hotel penetration still rising from a 57%-branded base, rising global disposable income/travel propensity, and secular growth in Asia-Pacific/Middle East middle-class travel demand

business.description: IHG's growth depends on maintaining brand and loyalty-programme preference against intensifying competitor marketing and alternative distribution channels (OTAs, Airbnb-style alternatives)
Pipeline growth depends on independent and institutional owners continuing to see attractive returns from IHG-branded conversions/new-builds versus competing brand families or unbranded operation

Middle East conflict caused RevPAR to fall ~19-50% in that sub-region (5% of system) during 2026, illustrating how geopolitical shocks in a concentrated market can dent regional performance even if offset elsewhere

business.risk: Reliance on third-party operators for brand delivery
business.description: IHG does not control day-to-day operations at the ~73% of system that is franchised, creating guest-experience consistency and reputational risk outside IHG's direct control

financial.description: Years of debt-funded share buybacks (cumulative returns of $5bn+ over five years targeted) have left equity at -$2.7bn to -$3.0bn; net debt:adjusted EBITDA targeted at 2.5-3.0x (2.63x at H1 2026, 2.89x per latest screen) leaves limited headroom if earnings deteriorate
Adjusted interest expense rose 16% YoY in H1 2026 ($106m vs $91m) as net debt increased; further buybacks or weaker FCF would pressure coverage
USD reporting currency against GBp-quoted shares and global fee streams denominated in local currencies creates translation noise (FX losses of $7m in H1 2026 vs gains of $79m in H1 2025)

regulatory.risk: Legal, regulatory and contractual complexity/litigation exposure
regulatory.description: Franchise agreement disputes, data privacy regulation (divergent global privacy/localisation requirements), and increasing regulatory enforcement variability are an explicitly flagged principal risk

Total carbon emissions rose 7.7% since 2019 as the estate grew, even as per-room intensity fell ~10-11%; transition cost and disclosure requirements could rise, and limited clean-energy infrastructure in some markets constrains mitigation

macro.description: Management explicitly flags tariffs, labour and tax policy pivots, escalating geopolitical tensions, and market/financial turbulence (cost of capital, supplier financial stress) as 2026-2028 risk themes
RevPAR and system growth are tied to business/leisure travel cycles; a global recession or sustained high rate environment would reduce RevPAR and slow owner investment in new signings
Growing dependency on third-party cloud/technology platforms and AI adoption increases exposure to cyberattack and data breach risk, explicitly named as an escalating principal risk

macro_factors.industry_outlook: Global hotel industry estimated at $750bn, historically growing faster than GDP (outpaced GDP growth in 19 of 26 years 2000-2025); Oxford Economics forecasts global hotel room nights to grow ~3.6% annually through 2035; global net new room supply grew at a 2.3% CAGR 2015-2025 and is expected to continue near that rate
macro_factors.cyclicality: Moderately cyclical - RevPAR and system growth track business/leisure travel demand and the broader economic cycle, but the fee-based, diversified-by-geography/segment/stay-occasion model (business, leisure, group travel) and heavy weighting to domestic/intra-regional travel provide relative resilience versus owned hotel operators
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Moderate - rising rates increase IHG's own adjusted interest expense on net debt and can dampen hotel owner investment appetite for new development/signings (financing costs for key money, construction, conversions)
macro_factors.currency_exposure: Reports in USD but has global fee streams in local currencies (GBP, EUR, RMB, etc.) and LSE-quoted shares in GBp; FX translation materially moves reported IFRS EPS in some periods
key_input_costs: Labor/talent costs (own corporate workforce and influence over managed-hotel staffing)
Marketing and loyalty programme investment (funded via System Fund)

recent_developments.event: H1 2026 results: revenue from reportable segments +7% to $1,255m, EBIT from reportable segments +10% to $665m, adjusted EPS +13% to 274.7c; fee margin up 120bps to 65.9%; net debt $3,663m (net debt:EBITDA 2.63x); on track for $1.2bn+ of 2026 shareholder returns

Middle East conflict caused regional RevPAR to fall sharply (~19% in Q2, deteriorating further through the period) in a sub-region representing 5% of global system size; management says the drag is expected to be fully offset by stronger demand elsewhere (Americas benefited from FIFA World Cup match locations, adding ~1.0%pt to Q2 Americas RevPAR)

Q1 2026 trading update: global RevPAR +4.4% (better than expected), confident of meeting consensus growth/profit forecasts; reached milestone of 7,000+ open hotels; $240m of the $950m 2026 buyback completed

Share buyback execution: 2026's $950m programme was 25% complete by May, 42% complete by end-H1, following $900m (2025), $800m (2024) and $750m (2023) programmes - a sustained multi-year pattern of debt/cash-funded buybacks
Completed the $900m FY2025 share buyback programme; combined with dividends, returned over $1.1bn to shareholders in 2025
Acquired Ruby, a premium urban lifestyle/micro-hotel brand, to expand IHG's Premium segment presence in city destinations, with plans to scale it from its European base into the Americas and Asia
Launched Noted Collection, a new premium collection brand, building on prior collection/conversion brand successes (voco, Garner)
IHG surpassed 1 million open rooms globally and opened a record 443 hotels in the year, with 694 signings taking the pipeline to 2,292 properties
Leadership change: Tejas Katre succeeded Wayne Hoare as Chief Human Resources Officer following Hoare's retirement; Nicholas Cadbury appointed Non-Executive Director (joined board March 2026)

Zacks Research downgraded IHG from Hold to Strong Sell, a contrarian move against the broader 'Moderate Buy' analyst consensus and recent price-target increases from Jefferies ($160 to $195, Buy) and Bernstein ($141 to $154, Market Perform)
Scheduled Q3 2026 trading update (not yet released as of this analysis date)

items.vs_prior: maintained; FY2025 outperformed the medium-term target
items.notes: Driven by operating leverage and ancillary fee stream step-ups

items.metric: EBIT (operating profit from reportable segments) growth

items.target: +12-15% CAGR (medium/long-term); +13% YOY in H1 2026, +16% in FY2025
items.vs_prior: maintained; FY2025 and H1 2026 both tracking within/above range
items.notes: FY2025 adjusted EPS growth of 16% exceeded the 12-15% target range

items.target: +5.0% YOY in H1 2026 (no explicit full-year numeric target disclosed; FY2025 adjusted net growth was 4.7%)
items.notes: Record H1 2026 openings (31.5k rooms/197 hotels) and signings (49.2k rooms/352 hotels), both +8% YOY on an organic basis excluding Ruby

items.target: $950m share buyback programme for FY2026 (42% complete at H1), plus growing ordinary dividend; combined returns of $1.2bn+ expected in 2026
items.notes: Would take cumulative five-year shareholder returns to more than $5bn; dividend raised 10% YoY for a fourth consecutive year (interim 64.5c, up from 58.6c)
2.63x at H1 2026; Board expects leverage to remain within target range given FY2026 growth/EBITDA expectations

items.vs_prior: maintained through Q1 and H1 2026 updates despite Middle East disruption
items.notes: Management reiterated confidence in meeting full-year consensus despite Middle East conflict drag, citing expected offsetting demand growth elsewhere

guidance.management_commentary: CEO Elie Maalouf said H1 2026's 'diverse global footprint and better-than-expected demand in most markets' delivered RevPAR growth of +4.1%, with US trading accelerating in Q2 and Greater China continuing to grow, while EMEAA performance was helped by strength outside the Middle East. He noted 'ongoing impacts from the Middle East conflict, including some wider disruption to international travel flows,' but expressed confidence these would be 'fully offset by growth in demand elsewhere,' citing the business model's geographic, chainscale and stay-occasion diversification. Management remains confident in the growth algorithm (RevPAR + net system growth -> HSD% fee revenue CAGR -> ~10% EBIT CAGR -> 12-15% adjusted EPS CAGR) and in delivering $1.2bn+ of FY2026 shareholder returns.

bull_case: Pure fee-based, asset-light model with ~65% fee margins and minimal incremental capital requirements supports high returns on invested capital and near-100%+ cash conversion, funding both growth investment and large, sustained shareholder returns

Visible, growing pipeline (~2,300-2,400 hotels, ~33% of current system size) and record openings/signings in 2025-2026 provide multi-year forward revenue visibility independent of near-term RevPAR swings

Diversification across geography (Americas/EMEAA/Greater China), chainscale (Luxury & Lifestyle to Essentials) and stay-occasion (business/leisure/groups) cushions localized shocks, as demonstrated by offsetting Middle East weakness with US/China strength in 2026

Expanding ancillary fee streams (co-brand cards, loyalty point sales, 160m+ member IHG One Rewards programme generating 66% of room nights) and newer higher-fee Luxury & Lifestyle brands (Six Senses, Regent, Ruby) support continued fee-margin expansion ahead of the 100-150bps/year medium-term target

Long-running track record of double-digit annual shareholder returns growth (10% dividend growth for four consecutive years, buyback programmes growing from $500m in 2022 to $950m in 2026, cumulative returns targeted above $5bn over five years)
bear_case: Negative shareholders' equity (-$2.7bn to -$3.0bn) from years of debt-funded buybacks leaves no balance-sheet cushion; continued buybacks at the top of the 2.5-3.0x leverage target range reduce flexibility if a demand shock or refinancing-cost increase hits simultaneously

Headline 'total revenue' figures ($5.2bn in FY2025) are dominated by pass-through System Fund and reimbursable revenue that is not IHG's economic income, creating a risk that investors unfamiliar with the model misjudge growth or valuation multiples off the wrong revenue base

Geopolitical/regional shocks (the 2026 Middle East conflict cutting regional RevPAR by ~20-50% in a 5%-of-system sub-region) show earnings can be hit by concentrated events outside management's control, even if diversification cushions the group level

As the third-largest of the major global hotel franchisors behind Marriott and Hilton, IHG competes in a fragmented, intensely competitive industry for both owner signings and guest loyalty, with Accor, Hyatt, Wyndham and Choice all pursuing similar conversion-led growth strategies

Valuation already reflects a strong growth and buyback narrative (consensus 'Moderate Buy' but with a wide analyst price-target range and at least one 'Strong Sell' rating in 2026), leaving limited room for error if RevPAR growth or system growth decelerates meaningfully
